per_depth.common_affordance: The statement directly supplies the complete decision rule: test each p1+p2 against T, then test the two stage totals, under a promise that exactly one case applies.
The statement exposes an exhaustive, directly checkable set of necessary lower bounds: p1+p2>T for a task certificate, or total stage load>T for a stage certificate.
the exhaustive promise that every impossible instance is covered by exactly one of the two simple local inequalities
The statement directly and exhaustively equates impossibility with checking either an individual p1+p2>T inequality or a total stage load>T inequality.
The certificate is completely determined by intrinsic necessary lower bounds: p1+p2>T certifies JOB i, while sum(p1)>T or sum(p2)>T certifies LOAD 1 or LOAD 2.
The certificate definitions deliberately decouple the constraints, so validity is determined entirely by additive duration lower bounds: `p1+p2>T` for a job or `sum(p_c)>T` for a machine.
The non-strict chain inequality makes the local contradiction test use p1+p2>T rather than also treating equality as impossible.
The geometry is completely characterized by additive length bounds: a local pair is feasible exactly when p1+p2<=T, and a category is packable exactly when its total span is at most T.
The constraints make every local product and every globally chained sequence a product of powers of two, so feasibility is decided by comparing an additive sum of p-values with T.
The explicit multiplicative power-of-two form of the local subsystem makes the local contradiction reducible to the single comparison p_{i,1}+p_{i,2}>T.
